answer: On a hot afternoon the sea breeze arrives as a sudden cool gust, and claimants report the minute the temperature drops, which must march inland at the speed of the front. A terrace by the shore feels it first, a canyon of streets channels it next, and the echo of the change reaches each house minutes after the last. A Sybil operator cannot fake the march, because inventing arrival times means predicting a front's speed better than the weather service itself.
